## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Pārāyanānugītigāthā* (Cnd 4), translated as "Concluding Verses of the Way to the Beyond," is a text in the *Cūḷaniddesa* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It consists of the concluding verses attached to the *Pārāyanavagga*, directly corresponding to Sutta Nipāta 5.19 (PTS Snp 219) and forming the root text explained in the canonical commentary *Pārāyanānugītigāthāniddesa* (Cnd 22) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records two translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus align the text across 108 matching passages in four Pali texts, with no cross-language matches recorded with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of Pali reuse occurs in its dedicated commentary in the *Cūḷaniddesa*, the *Pārāyanānugītigāthāniddesa* (Cnd 22), with 92 matching passages (including segments §15.1–16.4 matching §111.1–112.4) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records extensive identical text reuse with *Pārāyanānugītigāthā* (Snp 5.19) across segments §0.3–19.5, alongside minor shared passages with the *Hemakamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 12) and the later grammatical treatise *Saddanītippakaraṇaṃ (Padamālā)* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
